title: Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember isn't just a sequel - it's a culmination of everything Team Ninja has learned from Nioh, Ninja Gaiden, and Dead or Alive
text: The original Wo Long is an overlooked gem . Fast-paced, brutal, and compelling, the game made a name for itself amongst hardcore action-RPG aficionados because of its key gimmick: that basically every single attack could be deflected. While some criticised this because it made the game 'repetitive', I thought it was interesting and well-executed enough to carry you through the entire playtime. Augmented by a momentum mechanic that rethought stamina for the fast-paced fights, and a still best-in-class 'morale' system that encouraged exploration and completionism, Wo Long has a permanent place on my harddrive. title: The weird, wonderful world of Miles Buckle, Instagram's parallel universe of video games

The " here's Johnny " scene from The Shining, where Jack Nicholson terrorises Shelley Duvall, recreated in the stilted comedic style of The Sims 2 . The opening sequence of Twin Peaks told through the landscapes of SimCity 2000 – one of several "orthographic experiments" that Buckle has done using the most iconic Maxis game of my childhood. A low-poly Peter Finch doing the Oscar-winning "I'm a human being, god dammit!" monologue from Sidney Lumet's classic Network. title: Microsoft Reacts To Xbox Game Pass Rumor That Could Change The Service In A Big Way
text: Microsoft has released a statement in response to a new rumor that claims the company is considering a massive shakeup to Xbox Game Pass in 2027 that would include numerous significant changes. ResetEra user Slayven , who has accurately reported on unannounced Xbox news before , said the changes could include the bifurcation of Game Pass into two tiers: one with ads and one without. The tier with ads would be $13/month, while Game Pass without ads would cost $20/month, according to the report. Xbox Game Pass could see a big shakeup. That's $3/month less than Game Pass Ultimate currently, and the price cut is reportedly reflective of another big change: Microsoft is reportedly removing day-one new releases from Game Pass starting in the February-April window of 2027. The rumor also stated that cloud-streaming access is being taken out of Game Pass, but people can pay for a $6 add-on that gets you 25 hours. Additionally, the report said a Family Plan will be available for an extra $6/month. Beyond all of this, the report claimed there will be a tier of Game Pass that costs $15/month, and for that, people will get access to select titles in the Game Pass library, along with online multiplayer. Finally, it was reported that Microsoft will also offer a $11/month membership that provides access to online multiplayer alone. Microsoft responded to the rumor in a statement to GameSpot, originally obtained by Paul Tassi of Forbes . The statement reads: "We regularly test different Game Pass offerings and look at what works best for players in different markets. We don’t have any changes to announce today or plans that have been finalized. There are no changes to previously announced games coming to Game Pass Ultimate on day one." Not a random leaker Reputable leaker NateTheHate said on ResetEra that Slayven has a track record for accuracy, at least somewhat, so "the individual giving them information clearly has knowledge of some matters." However, NateTheHate did not corroborate the reporting. Slayven said on October 1, 2025 that Microsoft was raising the price of Game Pass Ultimate to $25--they were right about an increase, but it actually went up to $30/month . They were also right about the names changing from Game Pass Core to Game Pass Essential and Game Pass Standard to Game Pass Premium. They didn't get everything right, though, as Slayven said PC Game Pass was being removed, but it wasn't. In any event, this latest rumor of a massive Game Pass shakeup should be taken with a grain of salt until Microsoft officially makes an announcement. Game Pass has undergone big changes already While it remains to be seen if this rumor proves accurate, Xbox's new CEO, Asha Sharma, has already made efforts to shake up Game Pass. One of her first moves after becoming CEO in February 2026 was to cut the price and remove new Call of Duty games from the service when they release. Sharma previously said Game Pass was too expensive and that she had big changes in store for it. She also alluded to a longer-term vision after the price cuts. "Long term, we will evolve Game Pass into a more flexible system which will take time to test and learn around," she said. That sounds like exactly what the rumor is suggesting. If the rumor is correct, or even parts of it, the new evolution of Game Pass would offer more options and possibly become cheaper for those who are OK with ads. On the subject of ads, Microsoft just recently rolled out a test for an ad-supported version of cloud gaming , and it's not a stretch to imagine this could be expanded in new ways to help Game Pass reach more people by way of lower prices. Not everyone wants this , of course, and Microsoft is sure to face pushback just like other entertainment companies have for their own ad-based tiers of their own subscription services. With regards to removing day-one releases, Microsoft is already doing this with Call of Duty, as this year's Modern Warfare 4 won't be available on the service at launch. Getting access to all of Microsoft's first-party games at launch as part of Game Pass was previously one of the membership's top selling points. New Call of Duty games will not come to Game Pass until the following holiday season, so people shouldn't expect Modern Warfare 4 until late next year. Sharma has said she is considering a "range of options" for exclusives going forward, including "windowing" some games, and that could mean a lot of things for Game Pass and beyond. One possibility is that certain games are kept out of Game Pass at launch and for a period of time, similar to how movies are only available in theaters at first before coming to digital and streaming. The idea is that this pushes people to pay full price as opposed to getting access to new content as part of their membership right away. So far, it's just Call of Duty that is being "windowed" in Game Pass. Minecraft Dungeons II will launch into Game Pass this month, as will Gears of War: E-Day in October. 2027's Fable will be a day-one release, too, in February 2027. As for the cloud gaming changes, earlier this month, Microsoft announced that in November, the company will put limits on how many hours per month people can use the service. People can then pay more to unlock more time . In addition to making Game Pass more affordable, Sharma might look to partner with Netflix on some kind of bundle offering for Game Pass. Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters said he and Sharma have “kicked around ideas” for how Netflix and Xbox could work together on subscription bundles. Nothing has been confirmed, but Peters said he “wouldn’t eliminate any possibilities.” Speaking generally about Game Pass, Sharma has said one of her ambitions is to "fortify" the service with "clear differentiation and sustainable economics." Sharma is also trying to get Xbox as a platform and company back into a healthy place, and that has meant drastic cuts of late involving layoffs, studio divestitures, and game cancellations. In regards to growth, Sharma recently oversaw the signing of Hideo Kojima for his new game, Physint , which was previously in the works at PlayStation. The game was reportedly over budget and late , which contributed to PlayStation's decision to part ways with Kojima.

title: James Pond Legacy Situation Is More Than Meets The AI
text: Last month, System 3 Software released a trailer for James Pond Legacy, a four-game collection for Nintendo Switch 2. But the gameplay footage was largely overshadowed by accusations its developer used generative AI to create the game's promotional artwork and cover. System 3 followed this trailer up with a blog post asserting that generative AI was not used in the development process for James Pond Legacy, but some wires were evidently crossed. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CFggndxGZk0 If you go back and watch that trailer, it's not difficult to see why viewers pointed out the AI-like quality of the 3D characters adorning the game's box art and other promotional material. When System 3 responded to the accusations with the assertion that "no generative AI was used in the creation of the artwork," referring specifically to the Bovine Bomber character, this was based on the information it was given at the time by Antstream, the studio that handled the collection's actual development. "That was the statement that we were given at the time by Antstream," System 3 CEO Mark Cale told GameSpot during a call. "We weren't involved in the process. They supplied all of the artwork and they supplied, in the process, the [work-in-progress] illustration. All of that was given to us." Cale later provided GameSpot with the statement it received back in December from Antstream, well before the trailer was made public. "The art pipeline on some non-in-game assets includes algorithm-assisted depth and form translation: Original 2D concepts are input into a model to estimate volume and lighting, producing pseudo-3D drafts," reads the statement from Antstream. "Artists then manually repaint, re-render, and finalise all illustrations using this pipeline. The final assets are fully human-authored, with algorithms used only for intermediate visualisation." You may notice that the statement omits the term "AI," which led to some internal confusion. "We requested this [statement] for use across the board, including Steam, and to address applicable requirements under the EU Artificial Intelligence Act , including the transparency provisions that took effect on August 2, 2026," Cale explained. "Antstream now argues that, because we requested the statement for these purposes, we must have known the extent of their use of AI. However, their statement expressly describes the final assets as 'fully human-authored,' with algorithms used 'only for intermediate visualisation.'" Had the use of generative AI been made clearer prior to the publication of the trailer and the blog post, System 3 would have taken a different approach, Cale said. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FPypcOQ8SDQ "That doesn't say 'generative AI,'" Cale said. "And if they've used any generative AI at all, it should have been clear in that statement. That was the statement we were told to put on to Nintendo, to Steam, PS5, Xbox--any format we want to go based on that. The actual gameplay itself is, of course, all emulated anyway. And for me, I don't know the definition of how you're going to try to say something that's prompt-based [is] 'generative AI' versus algorithms. And so we honestly looked at that and took that honestly to [mean] there was no AI." GameSpot was unable to reach Antstream for comment during our time investigating the situation. Cale said he is far from wanting to throw Antstream under the bus for what happened. He explained the reason Antstream was contracted for the project was because it had done "a bloody good job" of emulating games for past compilations, such as The Last Ninja Collection. The situation for James Pond was a little different, though, with little in the way of existing concept art or other production designs to go on for the in-game supplemental materials. As someone wary, to put it mildly, of any generative AI usage in video games, I told Cale I would have preferred hand-drawn material created specifically for the collection based on past artwork, but Cale said it wasn't feasible. "All of the artwork that has been created within the Pond-verse has been based on art that's either on the box cover or characters that are in the game," he said. "And at the end of the day, if people think we're going to redraw, re-render to that quality, and have 20 or 30 people working two years on it, forget it: It's not going to happen. We wouldn't put the Pond-verse in there. The simple fact is, it would not match an investment versus a return. I'm only speaking for myself--I can't speak for Antstream--but if it was for me, I wouldn't do it, because I couldn't justify having 20 artists for a year create all of that in that way." Still, Cale said that full disclosure--and a clearer set of guidelines for what System 3 considers generative AI--should help to avoid another situation like this happening in the future. Having a set, and perhaps broader, definition for what constitutes generative AI will, at the very least, help prospective buyers know what they're purchasing. It won't completely solve the problem, though, as Cale mentioned the need to be careful about using the term "AI" to describe any element in a game--even some that have existed for decades. "AI's become such a swear word, and you should quote me on that!" Cale said. "So, you know, we're doing this other game. It's all been hand-done and everything, and I can't even say, 'Opponent AI's been tweaked to do this.' No, it's 'opponent behavior.' It's just madness! I just don't want to use the word 'AI' in anything, as far as I'm concerned, anymore." James Pond Legacy: The Pond is Not Enough doesn't have a final release date yet, but will launch exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2 at the end of October.

title: The Last Of Us Season 3 Is Probably The Final Season, HBO Says Yet Again
text: HBO boss Casey Bloys has once again said that the upcoming third season of The Last of Us is expected to be its last. He told Deadline that Season 3 is coming in 2027, though did not confirm when in the year. Asked if he still think it's the final season, Bloys said he believes showrunner Craig Mazin "has planned it as the final season." In January this year, Bloys was asked if Season 3 is going to be the last, and he said, "It certainly seems that way." However, at the time, Bloys admitted that a decision like that would come down to Mazin. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uLtkt8BonwM Before this, Mazin said that Season 4 was essential to bring the show to a conclusion. However, Bloys has indicated that the show may wrap up its run with Season 3 , which could be a longer season. “Craig is still working it out whether it will be two more seasons or one more long season. It hasn’t been decided yet, and I’m following Craig’s lead on that,” Bloys said in 2025. In a big shift for the series, franchise creator Naughty Dog is not involved creatively in Season 3 , and Neil Druckmann dropped out as a writer/director. People have speculated about what this could mean, but Druckmann, for his part, said he left the show to focus on his work on Naughty Dog's games. He is currently directing Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet , and if it's true that Naughty Dog is also making The Last of Us 3 , he's probably involved in that, too.

title: Xbox Game Pass Removes 8 More Games Very Soon
text: Microsoft has announced the second wave of removals from Xbox Game Pass this month, and eight more games are heading out soon. Earlier this month, Microsoft removed 10 games from Game Pass , so a total of 18 games are being removed this month alone. Titles set for removal on September 30 include Atomfall, Lara Croft and the Guardian of Light, Sifu, and Little Nightmares 2 Enhanced Edition. Other games getting dumped include SOPA Tale of the Stolen Potato, Sworn, Little Rocket Lab, and Terminull Brigade. title: PlayStation Plus Is Removing 7 Games Soon, So Play Them While You Can
text: A fresh batch of games are coming to the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog for Extra- and Premium-tier subscribers, but several games are also on their way out. While we don't have an exact date for their exit just yet, there'll be seven games in total leaving soon, so you only have a few weeks left to play one of the best survival-horrors of all time and a melodramatic gangland adventure where you can hit people really hard on the head with a baseball bat. PlayStation Plus Game Catalog games leaving soon These games are leaving the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog soon. Silent Hill 2 Yakuza: Like a Dragon Gloomhaven: Mercenaries Edition Jurassic World Evolution 2 Rogue Lords Lake Death Squared The biggest departure on the list is easily the Silent Hill 2 remake from Bloober Team, and it's leaving right before the start of spooky season. While the original Silent Hill 2 was long considered to be one of the greatest psychological-horror games of all time, the remake improved on it tremendously, offering more than just updated visuals and modernized gameplay. Dynamic combat is balanced by smarter enemy AI, while the titular Silent Hill is expanded with new locations and puzzles to create an explorable world full of suspense. Critically acclaimed upon its 2024 release, it's one of several new entries that have helped kickstart a Silent Hill renaissance . Not only did it feature a brand-new protagonist in the form of Ichiban Kasuga, but the gameplay also went from beat-'em-up brawling to turn-based RPG action. First arriving in late 2020, it's another great Yakuza game that combines a surprisingly heartfelt story with goofy moments and a likable cast of rogues. While the turn-based gameplay can be a grind--especially in the endgame--it's still worth checking out. Fans of the Yakuza franchise have eaten well since then, as we've gotten a sequel to Ichiban's first adventure, Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth, as well as several spin-off games and remakes. title: Kingdom Hearts’ Kairi Has Suffered Enough, Will Now Headshot You In Fortnite
text: For the longest time in the Kingdom Hearts series, Kairi has gotten the short end of the stick, but the franchise's upcoming crossover with Fortnite will finally let Kairi fans choose violence. A new trailer for Fortnite's ongoing Chapter 7 Season 4 shows the trio of Sora, Riku, and Kairi in action. The three sport their Kingdom Hearts 2 appearances, and each wields their own Keyblade. They're seen fighting Heartless (or Heartless-like?) enemies in an area resembling their home world of Destiny Islands, hinting that the ever-evolving Fortnite map will add the locale . It's all set to the Kingdom Hearts 2 theme "Sanctuary" by Utada Hikaru, which still slaps two decades later. There's no footage of the Destiny Islands trio wielding firearms, but Sora using a shotgun and Kairi blasting opponents with an assault rifle will be a sight to see when the skins drop later this week. It should be cathartic to a degree to play as Kairi in Fortnite, seeing how she's been treated in her own series. Kairi is often relegated to a damsel-in-distress role, and when Kingdom Hearts 3 ( spoilers ahead for that 2019 game) finally put her in an important position as a Guardian of Light, she... gets kidnapped again and is effectively killed off , leading Sora to literally break the laws of nature to save her. Kairi does have more to do as a playable character in the Kingdom Hearts 3 Re Mind DLC , and she serves as the protagonist of the Melody of Memory rhythm game. But arguably, that's not enough for fans to forgive the sins of the series and its use of Kairi. With Fortnite, Kairi fans can finally blow off steam by mowing down fools with a gun. The next major Fortnite update is expected to drop on Thursday, September 17, and with it should come Sora, Riku, Kairi, and Roxas. It's also expected that Sora's Kingdom Key will be added to the loot pool as a weapon.

title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation’s Director Kept Coming Back To The Witcher 3 For Inspiration
text: Between the release of Final Fantasy 7 in 1997 and the first chapter in the Remake trilogy in 2020, quite a few games have been released and have gone on to inspire developers. Final Fantasy 7 Revelation game director Naoki Hamaguchi is one such developer, as he explained that games like The Witcher 3 and Horizon helped inspire him and his team to deliver cinematic storytelling native to interactive media, as well as player agency through customizability and scalable world exploration. "Final Fantasy 6 was a very impactful title for me when I was playing the games when I was younger, when I was a child. But as a creator, I would say that The Witcher 3 would fill that role of what inspired game creation," Hamaguchi said to GameSpot. "When I started working on the Remake series, I would frequently go back to The Witcher 3 and just marvel at the things that that game excels at. It's a frequent one that I revisit." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LRA759MHPJs Hamaguchi added that the Final Fantasy 7 Remake team also wanted to take a different approach to storytelling, as they didn't just want to insert cutscenes into the game world. Hamaguchi says he studied how The Witcher 3 and Guerrilla's Horizon created cinematic pay-offs within the framework of their gameplay mechanics. "We do have to acknowledge that there are certain moments that bring satisfaction that can be only achieved by doing it within the video game medium," Hamaguchi explained. "I think that is exactly something that The Witcher 3 and games like Horizon were really excelling at, just delivering these satisfactory moments. They feel cinematic. That was something that we were trying to follow suit with." More than a decade after its release, The Witcher 3 is still considered one of the greatest open-world games of all time, and it's getting a massive remastered edition on September 29. Next year will also see the launch of an expansion, Songs of the Past , which should help with the long wait for The Witcher 4 . Fortunately, Final Fantasy fans won't have to wait too much longer for the final chapter in the remake series to land, as Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will launch for PC and consoles in April 2027 . Square Enix is aiming to make this the biggest game possible, with a "planetary scale" world to jump into. Beyond the main campaign to stop Sephiroth once and for all, there'll also be other activities to take part in, like some classic snowboarding fun . Interview conducted by Emma Fyffe .

title: 007 First Light’s Switch 2 Edition Delayed Yet Again, Here’s How Long You Have To Wait
text: Developer IO has confirmed that 007 First Light's Switch 2 edition has been delayed for a second time. It's now scheduled for March 2027. The studio said in a notice that First Light's Switch 2 version was delayed "to ensure we deliver the quality of experience players expect." "This additional time will go toward polishing the Nintendo Switch 2 performance of the game," IO said. First Light's Switch 2 version was playable at Gamescom recently, and IO said it was "thrilled by the positive feedback." The same demo will be at Tokyo Game Show this week in Japan. "Thank you for your patience, understanding, and continued support," IO said. First Light's Switch 2 version was originally set to launch alongside the console and PC editions in May, but was later delayed to Summer 2026. Another delay for the Switch 2 edition seemed likely given that Summer officially ends on September 22 and IO had not communicated a release date. Another reason another delay for the Switch 2 edition is not that surprising is because IO boss Hakan Abrak said back in May that the game needed "a bit more time to get it where we want it to be." At the time, Abrak said the game was now targeting late-Summer , but now it's been delayed to 2027. “We just want to make sure it’s good as it can be. I don’t want to hear it wasn’t a good version," Abrak told The Game Business . First Light sold more than 4 million copies and earned rave reviews. All the signs are pointing to a sequel , but it has not been officially announced yet.

title: Diablo 5 Doubles Down On The Darkness, But Hope Still Has A Place In Sanctuary
text: Diablo's world of Sanctuary isn't a top tourist destination, thanks to roaming monsters and demonic forces looking to corrupt humanity, and in Diablo 5 , everything has gone to hell--quite literally! Unlike the previous games in the series, which revolved around saving Sanctuary from Diablo and his Prime Evil Kin, Diablo 5 kicks off long after the Lord of Terror has conquered the land. In a world this bleak, how will players find the motivation to keep going when evil has already triumphed? Speaking to GameSpot at BlizzCon , the Diablo team discussed the grim setting of Diablo 5, as well as the glimmers of hope that still exist even during Diablo's post-apocalyptic reign. Human strongholds are no more, survivors are scattered across the land, and things look bleaker than usual for players when they set foot in that world. According to Blizzard, not only is Diablo 5 keeping the grim, dark atmosphere of Diablo 4 intact and doubling down on it, but the landscape will also reflect humanity's fall. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=blmyIDbxN2o&pp=0gcJCf4LAYcqIYzv "We need to tell a story of this apocalyptic Sanctuary, executive producer Matt Zitterman said. "Sanctuary is already a pretty dark place. How do we double down on that darkness and go even further? That's where the ideas of thinking about our world as being built in layers--a layer about the past, a layer about the present, and a layer about the future--really came to light. And with that, you know, the past is all about telling the stories of what happened to humanity when Diablo overtook Sanctuary." "A lot of games do this extremely well. There are little vignettes and stories that are told visually about how humans were trying to survive and ultimately failed, and we want those parts of the world, those parts of Sanctuary, to really tell that story." Zitterman added that Sanctuary's state in Diablo 5 is akin to a forest fire, both during and after a devastating blaze has swept through an area. "We use the metaphor of a forest fire a lot," Zitterman explained. "A forest fire ravages through a place and leaves behind a changed landscape. And we see that as kind of the parts of the world that represent the battlefields of where demons were fought, and ultimately, humans lost. But the landscape was forever changed by that invasion. And then there are the areas where there is still an active invasion." "We talked about the Dread Commanders as being the lieutenants in Diablo's army, and they are kind of roaming the world and controlling different parts of Sanctuary. When a Dread Commander is in an area in Sanctuary, it is an active invasion zone. It will feel like the forest fire is raging now. That represents the future of Sanctuary, should the player not succeed in kicking Diablo out. As you know, that's what Sanctuary will be forever. And so that's how we think about the world, as kind of three different layers of visual storytelling." But there is still some hope during these dark times, as senior production director Tiffany Wat outlined how the game's story about a march to reclaim a lost legacy will eventually push players to become the saviours of humanity. "Humanity is worth fighting for, and as the heir to Westmarch, not only are you fighting for humanity, but you're trying to claim back the kingdom that is yours," Wat said. "And that is where it's a little bit different from the past, where, as the Wanderer, you may not have as much of a personal stake in trying to defeat Diablo. But now, as the heir of Westmarch, this is your land; somebody else has conquered it, and that person happens to be Diablo. And so, as you're trying to survive and you're on the run, in the campaign, you're going to be meeting some survivors and forming that caravan, and it's going to start very small." "As you progress through the story and you find the opportunity to meet other survivors of the apocalypse, and hopefully they're trustworthy enough to join you in your caravan. There's a lot of great visual storytelling there as you're progressing through the game, fighting back the darkness, and your campfire is growing because your caravan is growing, right? So if a jeweler joins you, they're going to bring their wagon. If a blacksmith joins you, then the wagon circle will grow. And I love Oregon Trail, so I think this is a really cool metaphor. I think as you're traveling through the dark world, just the idea that you are making progress and that you're going to hopefully have an opportunity to become victorious in the end, I mean, that's what you're fighting for." Blizzard has big plans for Diablo 5 ahead of its 2029 launch, as it seeks to bring the best of previous games in the series to this new adventure . Fans of the loot grind can look forward to chasing down set items , and with so many classes to choose from , expect plenty of reasons to start a fresh run in Sanctuary.

title: WoW Devs Confirm Paladins Are A “Dad Class”
text: World of Warcraft has plenty of classes for players to choose from, but according to the game's senior game designer, Josh Greenfield, there's one class that has earned a very specific reputation. Speaking to GameSpot at BlizzCon , Greenfield and senior art director Jeff Parrott discussed their favorite and most-played classes. While Parrott confirmed that his is Hunter, Greenfield's infamous inclination toward the Paladin was discussed a little more in depth. He said that the Paladin is "certainly" a dad class, adding, "You know, I'm not a dad, I'm a dog dad, but I've got the dad bod, so Paladin is totally a dad class." So, straight from a World of Warcraft developer: Paladin is officially a dad class. His choice certainly fits the stereotype, since Paladins are heavily armored, can heal their allies, protect their party, and generally have the sort of dependable, responsible toolkit you'd expect from the class entrusted with keeping everyone else alive while still dealing impressive damage. Of course, being a Paladin isn't actually restricted to dads, but if you've ever encountered a Paladin player who seems particularly enthusiastic about keeping the party organized, now you know why. It's only a matter of time before Paladins start asking to take care of everyone's passport in the departure lounge. World of Warcraft Forever launches November 4, with a playable beta going live on September 17.

title: The WoW Forever Beta Starts This Week, Here’s How To Get Access
text: At this year's BlizzCon , Blizzard announced a new version of World of Warcraft Classic, called World of Warcraft Forever. Blizzard says WoW Forever is "built as a new permanent home alongside modern and Classic WoW." It's set after the events of Warcraft III Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom but before Molten Core, and sends players back to the original continents with a cap at level 60. There are new stories, a new class, and over 1,000 new quests in the title. With World of Warcraft Forever launching on November 4, a beta is due to start this week. There are a few ways you can gain access, so here's all you need to know. https://youtu.be/uQuKE0KDgiM WoW Forever beta start and end times The World of Warcraft Forever beta will run from Thursday, September 17 , to October 21, 2026 . There are no official start times just yet, although Blizzard often rolls its updates out between 11 AM and 2 PM ET, so we'd expect the beta to become available around then. How to access the WoW Forever beta There are a few ways you can gain access to the WoW Forever beta, although preordering and buying specific packs are the only guaranteed ways. Beta access is including with the Skyborne Epic Pack and Warcraft Forever Collection. The Skyborne Epic Pack is priced at $59.99 / £51.99, and the Warcraft Forever Collection is priced at $79.99 / £69.99, and both can be bought from the Battle.net store . You can also head to the WoW Forever website and opt-in to the beta, although this is not a guaranteed method of entry. The only way to guarantee entry is by preordering one of the above packs. However, you don't need to buy these packs to get entry to WoW Forever when it releases. That's included with your World of Warcraft subscription or game time. However, if you want access to the new Skyborne race, you'll have to upgrade. WoW Forever early name reservation You'll be able to reserve your WoW Forever name from October 27 through November 3, 2026, and that's included with any upgrade purchase. You can create and customize up to three characters during this period, and character names are reserved on a first-come, first-served basis. WoW Forever beta level cap While WoW Forever will be capped at level 60, the beta will initially be capped at level 20, increasing to level 30 after a few weeks. There's a host of new content coming with WoW Forever, including the Skyborne race, new dungeons, new raids, and an additional PvP battleground. It'll be released on November 4.

title: Diablo 5 Is Bringing Back Set Items, But Wants To Avoid Their Biggest Problem
text: One of the most satisfying things about the Diablo games is their loot grind, and in Diablo 5 , Blizzard has plans to keep you clicking enemies to death for a long time in pursuit of an elusive piece of armor or weapon. While it's still early days in terms of how itemization will be handled in the game, Blizzard has confirmed that gear-based sets will return. Set items were originally absent from Diablo 4 when the game launched in 2023, although set bonuses were later added through the Talisman system. Instead of armor collections, players could equip passive bonuses, set effects, and unique powers without needing to replace their current gear. "Something we talk about a lot on the team is we want Diablo 5 to be a game that feels like it has elements for you, regardless of which Diablo game was your favorite," executive producer Matt Zitterman said to GameSpot at BlizzCon . "Clearly, there's some inspiration being taken from Diablo 2 there, but we're also looking at Diablo 4 and the successes we've had there, and are pulling forward ideas from there as well as Diablo 3. "I think for us, Diablo 5 represents this really special moment in the franchise's history where we get to look at the past and bring forward things that feel really familiar, but give them a fresh take." https://youtu.be/Y8HaSFXR7tU "We want to bring set items back. The set system in Diablo 4 worked really well for that game, but something about the way that set items worked in Diablo 2 and Diablo 3, they create kind of like a little quest, right? You want to go like you're on a long-term journey to collect the pieces of this set to unlock something really important about the build you're chasing. We want to bring that forward into Diablo 5. We want to create moments where players feel motivated, not just by a quest log, but by the loot chase. And I think set items, done right, do a really great job of that. We have ideas about how we can overcome some of the challenges of set items, narrowing the itemization game more than broadening it." For more on Diablo 5--which won't be out until 2029 --you can read up on how Blizzard wants to make combat feel more visceral than ever before, why the studio went for a new numbered game instead of another Diablo 4 expansion, and how you'll have a broader selection of classes to choose from when you return to Sanctuary.

title: The Best Overwatch Heroes, According To Blizzard
text: If you've ever wondered which Overwatch heroes the people actually making the game enjoy playing, the answer is surprisingly varied. At BlizzCon 2026 , GameSpot spoke with Overwatch game director Aaron Keller and associate game director Alec Dawson about their personal favorites, their original mains, and the newer heroes they think you should be playing. Here are the best Overwatch heroes according to Blizzard developers: Lucio For Dawson, it all started with Lucio. "My first main, like, 'I want to play this character all the time,' was Lucio, he said. That's mostly down to Lucio's impressive movement, he explained. "When there's a character with very fluid mobility, I'm like, 'I'm going to lock in and learn as much as I can about this hero.'" Lucio's mobility is one of the defining things about his kit. He can wall ride, allowing him to move quickly around the map by chaining movement across walls rather than taking the ground approach. His Crossfade also gives him an area-of-effect speed boost which applies to any teammates within the radius. Combined with wall riding, this makes him especially good at quickly repositioning, escaping danger, chasing enemies, or returning to the point after death, as Dawson agrees. "I think Lucio just spoke to me on a level--I was like, 'Wait, I can do all of those things?' This guy's slide-sliding around walls! That was awesome from the start." And yes, you can count on it that Dawson has used Lucio's Soundwave to boop more than a few opponents down the well in Ilios. Tracer For Aaron Keller, his original main was Tracer. As someone who has been working on Overwatch from its inception, Keller's endorsement of the hero from the original roster is glowing. "I don't know if I have a main now, but my first was probably Tracer," he explained. "I just loved the mechanics. I feel like the kit is almost perfect, the way that it works." Tracer's kit is built around speed, mobility, and constant repositioning, which helps to explain why Keller finds it "almost perfect." Using her Blink ability, she can teleport a short distance, and it has multiple charges to escape danger quickly. She can then hit her Recall ability to essentially rewind to where she was a few moments earlier, restoring her previous health and ammo. Then there are her Pulse Pistols, which do huge damage at close range. It's that coherence and synchronicity that Keller loves. While he ends up taking the tank role pretty often these days, when he's playing damage, he'll opt for Tracer, although he admits, "I'm a lot worse at damage than I used to be." Reinhardt, Winston, Zayra, and Orisa When he is playing tank, Keller has several favorites rather than one definitive main. "I typically queue flex now, which means I typically queue tank now, is what happens. So, I rotate through a few of the tanks, between Reinhardt, Winston, I love playing Zarya. I'll play Orisa, also," he explained. If you're wondering which tanks have the seal of approval from one of Overwatch's key developers, that's Keller's shortlist. Doctrine When it comes to the newer heroes, Dawson singled out Doctrine as an example of the development team getting many different elements right at once. "Doctrine is a wonderful example of taking an art visual archetype that we hadn't explored yet, this techno-vampire, making it the Overwatch version of that, with all the gameplay bundled together for his drones," he said. "I thought that was just a really perfect sandwich of things all coming together." He's not alone in his admiration for Doctrine, though, as Keller agreed with him. "It's like this amazing combination of backstory, visuals, and gameplay that really supports this, sort of, vampire fantasy," he added. Doctrine takes the classic vampire concept and mixes it with Overwatch's futuristic sci-fi world. Instead of making a traditionally supernatural vampire, Blizzard created the "techno-vampire" by combining classic vampire imagery with futuristic technology. Doctrine has the seal of approval from both developers. That's probably as close as you can get to an official developer-certified hero recommendation. Shion Dawson's personal favorite among the newer heroes is Shion. "I think the one that I personally vibe with the most, 'cause it was just over the top, is Shion," he noted. And the developers apparently knew exactly what kind of hero they wanted Shion to be from the beginning. "From the very get-go we were basing this off some action movies; we need to kick a motorcycle from the air. It was like we're going crazy with this hero," Dawson explained. It seems Shion's personality is something that the developers feel connects her to players. "She just had that personality that's, sort of, villainous to her that I think also struck a really nice chord with people." It's those over-the-top, action-movie-inspired, slightly villainous elements that Dawson thinks resonate particularly well with players. Her personality matches the extravagance of her concept, and she's certainly not designed to be understated. Emre Keller's pick of the newer heroes is a little less flashy, but that's exactly where his praise is aimed. "I think the primary file of Emre feels so good," he explained. That primary fire is Emre's Synthetic Burst Rifle, a three-round burst weapon. That straightforward, satisfying burst-rifle shooting makes Emre easy to learn how to play. "Overwatch is a first-person shooter, so you just want a weapon like that in the game," Keller explained. "He might not be the flashiest character that we've got, but he has really resonated with a lot of players, and I think one of the reasons is that primary fire." While these heroes come highly recommended, they didn't always function in the way that you see today. Tracer used to shoot lasers from her eyes , while two of Overwatch's most-criticized characters are getting a rework .

title: Blizzard Says Diablo 5 Was Too Big To Be A Diablo 4 Expansion
text: Diablo 4 is far from dead, but don't expect any new expansions for the game going forward. Instead, Blizzard is preparing to tell the darkest story yet in Diablo 5 , one that required a new numbered game to properly reintroduce Diablo himself back to the series, following his defeat in 2012's Diablo 3. Currently aiming for a 2029 release , this would mean that players are in for a relatively short wait for a new Diablo game--compared to previous releases--as Diablo 5 will arrive a mere six years after Diablo 4. Speaking to GameSpot at BlizzCon , Diablo senior production director Tiffany Wat and executive producer Matt Zitterman explained that it made sense for Blizzard to move to a new Diablo so that the studio could make structural changes to the game--changes that would have been very challenging to pull off within the framework of a Diablo 4 expansion. "It really started by looking at who our players are," Zitterman said. "Who are Diablo players? Why are they playing Diablo? What do they want out of a Diablo game? That is a really critical step in the early conceptual phase for a game, even before you're thinking about, like, 'Gosh, should we make this an expansion? Should we make it a sequel? How do we do this?' Looking at past examples, looking at what's working well in Diablo 4, where there are opportunities for improvement, and we kind of build our ambition for the game at the conceptual phase through those avenues of information." https://youtu.be/Y8HaSFXR7tU "And as we started to understand and kind of solidify what that ambition was, it became very clear to us pretty early that in order to achieve what we wanted to achieve with this game, we needed to make some more deeply structural changes to the way the game works, changes that are just frankly hard to do in an expansion. Again, it's all about figuring out what the best way is to make the best Diablo game we can for players. Diablo is the main villain. Diablo is the guy that we want to tell a real story about. We want to tell a story that's on par with--and hopefully exceeds--the story we told with Lilith and Mephisto." "And to do that in an expansion just didn't feel right. We needed to give him his own game." Player feedback also plays a vital role in the development of Diablo 5, and Zitterman said that by announcing the game this early, Blizzard could make important changes well ahead of the game's eventual launch. "If we didn't announce now and we kind of held back until we were much further along in development, at that point, it's much harder to take that feedback and use it to make those really important changes and refinements to the game throughout development," Zitterman explained. For more on Diablo 5, you can learn how combat could be even more ferocious , how the game will offer more character classes than ever , and how the Plague Knight uses the grossest powers to stay a step ahead of Diablo's demonic armies.

title: Wardogs Devs Are Watching Economy Cheaters Like Hawks
text: With the FPS Wardogs dominating the Steam charts, developer Bulkhead is paying close attention to the game's various systems. The studio recently dropped a new patch that makes some necessary changes for server stability, while confirming that the team has their eyes on cheaters and exploiters. As part of Patch 0.11 , which came out on September 14, Bulkhead announced that should any dogs of war take advantage of Wardogs' economy by farming servers, they'll find themselves either temporarily or permanently banned from the game. "As an early access game, we’re not perfect, and we never will be," Bulkhead said in the patch notes. "But if you do find something and take advantage of it, we have decided to come down hard." To be specific, Bulkhead outlined three different scenarios that will come with three different repercussions depending on the type of exploit you partake in. Scenario 1: Stockpiling money by abusing cash exploits and bugs will result in a timed ban, with the length determined by whether you were banned previously. Your cash and experience will get reset, too. Scenario 2: Showing economy exploits through tutorial content will be treated as "advertising cheats," resulting in a permanent ban. However, if you happen to stumble upon an exploit and share that with Bulkhead on Discord or social media, that'll be seen as an "alert," which prevents you from being permanently banned. Scenario 3: If you're farming experience via server exploits, which Bulkhead says will result in "the most serious bans," your account will get banned permanently. The studio clarified, though, that it's open to feedback on this policy, stating that these positions could change if enough people believe they're too harsh. "In the very early stages of finding these issues you may find yourself getting away with it, but it doesn't take long for our backend data to flag abusers," Bulkhead said, "Effectively, if you find something and you then keep doing it, over and over again, that is abuse of an exploit. If you figure something out and test it once or twice, no biggy, thanks for helping us QA." Wardogs is currently Steam's hottest game right now, with over 320,000 people playing at the time of writing. It didn't have the smoothest of starts , but the kinks are getting ironed out as the days go on. Players are a little riled up at the moment, though, particularly because people don't know how to close the door behind them .

title: How WoW Forever Handles Its Massive Set Of New Quests
text: One of the big announcements at BlizzCon was WoW Forever , the next iteration of offering a classic-style WoW experience. Blizzard is hoping to draw players back to the OG WoW in a number of ways, including with the introduction of 1,000+ new quests. GameSpot caught up with Blizzard senior game designer Josh Greenfield to discuss this, along with why the game's OG quests--from 22 years ago--still resonate today. If Blizzard is adding 1,000 more quests to WoW with the update, how many does that bring the game up to in total? It's a tricky question to answer, Greenfield said, in part because some of WoW's original quests are "tracking quests," but if you're counting "actual playable quests," the game has around 3,000 to 3,500. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IEMrosrAVH0 So with 1,000+ more added of actual playable quests, that's a significant increase. WoW Forever also adds four new zones, and each of these has between 50 and 200 quests, so that's where many will come from. Additionally, the existing zones have been "glowed up," with the Wetlands and Azshara, specifically, getting a "lot of new quests to round them out as zones." "Every nook and cranny, you're going to find something, even from like level five ... onward, you're going to start seeing new stuff," Greenfield said. Also in our interview, we asked how Blizzard came up with the inspirations for the 1,000 new quests, and if there might be a new version of The Green Hills of Stranglethorn, which is regarded as perhaps the game's worst quest. Greenfield said that was "kind of a terrible quest," but it still has charm and remains memorable even to this day. A lot of the original WoW is full of similarly memorable and "super iconic" quests, Greenfield said, and Blizzard is keen to carry the torch forward with WoW Forever. "I think a lot of those quests explored the world at a very like ground level, and they they told stories at a very like ground level, a very like relatable level. You know, 'I am not the hero, I am a hero, and I'm going on this adventure with my dented shield and rusty sword.' And, you know, like things like The Missing Diplomat and things like that, like being able to kind of jet-set around the world and talk to different people and learn more about the cultures of each of these different zones, and learn a mystery and try and unravel a mystery." Greenfield teased that Blizzard might "help finish unraveling that mystery" in WoW Forever. He went on to say some of the original WoW's quests were dark and grim, and Blizzard is embracing that philosophy with a lot of the new quests. "Even Zephyr Isle, it's in the sky, it's nice and bright, but it's the story once you get into it, it's not it's not all, you know, sunshine and rainbows up there. It can be a little little hard," he said. WoW Forever releases on November 4. In addition to the new zones and quests, players can expected update class designs, revamped systems, visual and gameplay improvements, and an expanded list of race and class options. Players can access WoW Forever via their existing WoW subscription. However, players can buy the $80 Warcraft Forever Collection to receive the new Skyborne race, beta access, and early name reservation for WoW Forever. The Collection also includes Warcraft III: Reforged and Warcraft III: Reforged Forsaken Kingdom

title: Crazy Taxi Gets Crazier With Crazy Ex-Girlfriend Writers For New Movie
text: The Crazy Taxi franchise isn't just getting a brand-new game next year ; it's also getting a live-action movie. Netflix and Sega have announced a new partnership that will see a Crazy Taxi film coming to the streaming service in 2027. Dan Gregor and Doug Mand are penning the comedy's screenplay, after previously working together on Naked Gun (2025), Crazy Ex-Girlfriend, and How I Met Your Mother. There's no director attached to the project, yet. However, Original Film's Neal H. Moritz and Toby Ascher are producing the Crazy Taxi movie, alongside Sonic the Hedgehog series producer Toru Nakahara. "This film is for anyone who's spent hours behind the wheel of a yellow cab on their Dreamcast, with the music cranked up, smashing through everything in sight just to make the next fare," said Moritz and Ascher in the Netflix press release . The Netflix and Sega collaboration also includes a new Sonic animated show aimed at "an upper preschool audience," as well as a live-action movie based on Stranger Than Heaven . The latter is the newest game from developer RGG Studio--known for the Yakuza and Like A Dragon titles. Meanwhile, it will be intriguing to see how much the Crazy Taxi movie ties into Crazy Taxi: World Tour. The new arcade racing game will feature lore this time , such as driver backstories for why they got behind the wheel in the first place. Fascinatingly enough, Sega has been trying to get a Crazy Taxi movie out on the road for basically two decades. In fact, Superman and The Goonies director Richard Donner was attached to direct the adaptation at one point. Top 10 Highest Highest-Grossing Video Game Movies View Images

title: Diablo 5 Isn’t Reinventing The Combat Wheel, It’s Making It Spin Even Faster
text: Combat has grown massively between each numbered Diablo game, and for Diablo 5 , Blizzard is aiming to once again elevate those gameplay mechanics to new heights. "Fundamentally, we're an isometric action-RPG, and we're not looking to shake that up with Diablo 5," executive producer Matt Zitterman said to GameSpot at BlizzCon 2026 . "We're looking to improve on it, evolve it, and we have some great, interesting ideas about how to make combat feel even more visceral, even more action-forward. Kind of continuing to build on the success of that fast combat that started in Diablo 3, improved in Diablo 4, and we want to take it even further in Diablo 5. That's really what we're focused on from a combat and gameplay perspective." Zitterman added that Blizzard was also looking to the past for inspiration, picking the best elements from those games and building them into Diablo 5. "Something we talk about a lot on the team is we want Diablo 5 to be a game that feels like it has elements for you, regardless of which Diablo game was your favorite," Zitterman said. "We talk a lot about itemization in the game. Clearly, there's some inspiration being taken from Diablo 2 there, but we're also looking at Diablo 4 and the successes we've had there, and pulling forward ideas from there as well as Diablo 3. I think for us, Diablo 5 represents this really special moment in the franchise's history where we get to look at the past and bring forward things that feel really familiar, but give them a fresh take." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y8HaSFXR7tU Diablo 5 will launch in 2029 , and this time, Diablo has finally won. Set decades after the Lord of Terror successfully conquered Sanctuary, there's no safe harbor or stronghold to retreat to this time, as players have to keep on the move and recruit allies to their caravan of survivors. Diablo 5 will also give players more character classes to choose from than ever before, including the Monk, Demon Hunter, and the all-new Plague Knight that is empowered by spreading disease and pestilence across the battlefield.

title: Overwatch’s Tracer Once Shot Lasers From Her Eyes, And It Could Happen Again
text: If early iterations of characters had survived the development process, Tracer could have been a very different Overwatch hero. Speaking to GameSpot at BlizzCon 2026 , game director Aaron Keller mentioned that he had been playing Overwatch since 2013, "since Tracer was shooting lasers out of her eyes." When questioned about such a strange sequence of words, Keller explained that the bizarre version of Tracer came from the first days of Overwatch's engine development in late 2013. "When we were creating the Overwatch engine, you know, so this is late 2013, the first day we got Tracer in we all ran around but we didn't actually have a projectile system yet," he added. "So when you would fire, just like straight out of her eyes, [it was] two red lines." There weren't even any proper visual effects involved at that point. According to Keller, it was "literally two red lines," because the game was firing the weapon from the camera's position. "And so we had a blast running around, just shooting lasers at each others," he recalled. While the laser-eyed Tracer was ultimately replaced by the pulse pistols players know today, the idea apparently hasn't been completely banished from Blizzard's considerations. When asked whether the team might ever bring back a hero capable of shooting lasers from their eyes, associate game director Alec Dawson responded positively. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gK877kcyMTY "I think shooting lasers out of your eyes is pretty cool. Yeah, we can figure something out," he said. If Overwatch can finally have Jetpack Cat flying around the map, it can certainly have its roster stretched to accommodate laser beam eyes. "I think the possibilities are endless," Dawson added. He also joked that GameSpot's Jessica Cogswell should take credit if a future hero suddenly starts firing lasers from their eyes. So, while Blizzard hasn't announced a laser-eyed hero, the idea was explicitly floated around during our interview, and the developers certainly didn't seem opposed to it. And honestly, after a decade of Overwatch, a hero shooting lasers out of their face might still be one of the least strange things Blizzard could add. Overwatch's next character is Doctrine , while two existing heroes are getting substantial reworks .

title: Wardogs Players Really Want You To Close The Doors … Or Else
text: The hottest game on PC right now is Wardogs , the Battlefield-like mass multiplayer FPS by developer Bulkhead that's soaring up the Steam charts. While it may not be as hot as the game itself, the game's subreddit is full of hotheads demanding you do one teeny-tiny thing. Close. The. Doors. Behind. You. Released in a closed beta state in August 2026 before entering early access in September 2026, Wardogs has taken PC gaming by storm. It's not only the number-one trending game according to SteamDB, with an all-time peak of 428,666 concurrent players on September 13 , but it's also the fourth-most-played game on Steam , trailing behind Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, and PUBG: Battlegrounds. Folks can't get enough of being a dog of war. Something folks would love to get enough of, though? Players leaving those gosh-darn doors and gates open when venturing out onto the battlefield. All over the official Wardogs subreddit are a ton of players decrying the carelessness of other players when it comes to not closing doors and gates behind them. Redditor demonmit1 posted on September 14 , pleading for people to stop building so many gates and close the ones they open. "If you're helping build a FOB, please… We only need one air locked gate for logistics," demonmit1 said. "No one closes them anyways, so adding more is not good. Stop it. If someone wants to leave the base, they can jump over a wall. They don't need to leave through a door they'll forget to close." https://www.reddit.com/r/WarDogs/comments/1wdpm7n/close_your_fob_gates_please/ "[PSA]: stop leaving my doors and gates open at my fobs," wrote Redditor novastar17 on September 12 . "i have been trying to build mortar complexes and random allies come open doors and let enemies in to just wipe all of us while im busy building. stop that, thanks." "There should be upgraded doors / gates that auto shut after a few seconds," user GOpencyprep suggested on August 23 in a very potty-mouthed Reddit post. "Or teammates who forget to close the door behind them should be fired into the sun...one or the other. Seriously though this is a problem." What these FOBBs, or Forward Operating Base builders , are talking about are the doors and gates you can add when constructing bases that act as central operating hubs for your team. These FOBs allow you to create fortified defenses, as well as construct weapons and other armaments to keep your team ready for when the fighting gets particularly intense. Unfortunately, because the doors and the gates don't close behind you once opened, this gives the enemy team the opportunity to waltz in, shoot up the place, and leave as if they were invited in the first place. Even though only you and your teammates can open and close doors and gates, meaning the enemy can't just pry your FOB open, leaving any access point open leaves you, ahem, open to a raid. You can imagine how frustrating this would be. https://www.reddit.com/r/WarDogs/comments/1wf7gwf/friendly_tutorial_on_how_to_close_doors/ "While Servers are down CLOSE THE DAMN DOORS," Redditor xMrStonex put it bluntly on September 14 . "Title. Thank you." "I get killed so often when using mortars or working on the FOB, because lazy people can't be bothered to close the door when they leave the FOB," Automatic_Reach_32 suggested on September 14 . "You can't force people to close the doors, but I think this could be helped with some monetary encouragement. Pay people if they close the door behind them! Nothing game changing, something modest like the revive / heal tips, $15 to players who close the door, reward good behavour!!" "I just have to say one thing," Icy-Sock-2388 said in the title of their September 5 Reddit post . "CLOSE THE F***ING DOORS! Countless times now I've meticulously spent tens of thousands to rapidly build a mortar, AA, and respawn fob...only for it to be taken by the enemy because they casually walked through the front door, past the multi-layered airlocks, into the tower airlock, and then into the fob airlock room because EVERY one of those doors was open." There have been some threats in the subreddit , too! It's really just people announcing that, if you leave a FOB door or gate open, you'll get a chest full of lead from your own team if the enemy team hasn't pumped you full of it already. Clearly, no one wants to let the AC out and the enemies in. Speaking of being let in, Wardogs suffered brutal server queues once it entered early access. Thankfully, Bulkhead released a hotfix that kinda-sorta addresses the long server wait times, but you may still encounter the dreaded WD-L014 Error Code. We've broken down how to get past that so you can be a dog of war again.

title: The Triple-I Initiative Showcase Is Getting A Second Event In 2026
text: The Triple-I Initiative Showcase is officially coming back on October 8 at 9 AM PT / 12 PM ET , and this second instalment of the show will once again offer plenty of trailers and announcements from a wide variety of publishers and developers. Since the first presentation kicked off in 2024, the Triple-I Initiative has been an annual event, but the organizers say they have even more to show next month with a second dose of back-to-back video game trailers. Viewers can expect eight exclusive world premieres from studios such as Team17, Amanita Design, Strange Scaffold, and Norsfell, as well as reveals for Dave the Diver, Brotato, Chained Together, Risk of Rain 2, and Windrose. The showcase will run for around 45 minutes, and there'll also be news for games like Hela: of Mice and Magic, Militsioner, the new Among Us title, Pony Island 2: Panda Circus, Haunted Paws, and Outward 2. As usual, you can catch it live through the Triple-I Initiative's usual channels, like YouTube and Twitch . https://youtu.be/SUQZF72d92A The April showcase was a pretty impressive one from the Triple-I Initiative, as it featured back-to-back trailers for Risk of Rain 2 DLC, a darkly creative typing game called Final Sentence, and Castlevania: Belmont's Curse. As with several other video game showcases, the Triple-I Initiative has adopted a format that focuses purely on game trailers, with no adverts or sponsors wedged between them. Organized by Evil Empire--the developers behind the new Castlevania game that's out in October--the presentation is designed to offer high visibility for a curated selection of games from various creative teams.

title: The Last Of Us 2 Multiplayer Mod Canceled “On Behalf Of Sony,” Dev Says
text: Naughty Dog's The Last of Us franchise featured a multiplayer mode in Factions, and while the studio planned to add multiplayer to the sequel, it abandoned those ambitions before release. A modder spent months this year working on a multiplayer mod for The Last of Us 2, but its lead has now said it's not going to be released due to a request from Sony to shut it down. Modder @Speclizer_ said on social media that the mod was due to launch this month. However, they said they "recently received a letter on behalf of Sony Interactive Entertainment requesting for the mod not to be released." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0_hZQn8_1WA Speclizer said this is an "extremely sad" development, but they hope people who supported the project will stick with them for the next one. Their next project will be "something of my own" as opposed to an extension of an existing game. "Thank you all for the incredible amount of support over the last year. I hope to bring you something bigger and better soon!" Speclizer said. GameSpot has contacted Sony in an attempt to get more details. Naughty Dog was set to expand The Last of Us into an online multiplayer experience in a very big way with The Last of Us Online. The game was in development for years with significant resources dedicated to it, and it was reportedly almost ready for release . However, in December 2023, Naughty Dog canceled the game , saying at the time that it was going to focus on single-player games instead. Also at that time, Naughty Dog confirmed that it had two single-player games in development. One has been revealed to be Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, while the other remains a mystery; many believe it's The Last of Us 3 . In other Naughty Dog-related news, studio head Neil Druckmann has confirmed that the studio has no creative involvement in the upcoming third season of HBO's The Last of Us . This is a big change, as Druckmann himself was personally and directly involved in the previous two seasons.

title: Red Dead 2 Actor Shares A Gross Secret About The Game
text: Actor Roger Clark played Arthur Morgan in Rockstar's celebrated 2018 Western Red Dead Redemption 2, and his performance was memorable for many reasons. In the game, Arthur suffers from tuberculosis, and he coughs a lot as a result. Was it challenging for Clark to perform those sequences in particular? Yes, but it was "not as bad as you'd think," Clark said in a recent interview, in part because sometimes Clark recorded when he himself had a bad cough. Clark told Cade Onder that he had "five years to spread it out," regarding his voice-capture performance in Red Dead 2, and that's part of the reason why it wasn't as difficult as you might imagine. Additionally, Clark said if he was performing a "really bad coughing scene," this would be saved for the end of a given recording day, when his voice was already hoarse from all the work. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ceGnING8zhg Beyond this, Clark said over that five-year period, when he recorded his lines, he, like most people, got sick--and he used this to his benefit. "In five years, there's plenty of colds. There was a lot of data we got that was pretty damn genuine. […] I'd be like 'Hey, I've got a cold, let me get in there.' And they'd be like, 'Okay.' […] Nice good bit of phlegm," he said. In addition to his leading role in Red Dead 2, Clark is known for his roles in the games Fort Solis, Rosewater, and Marathon. He won Best Performance for his role as Arthur Morgan at The Game Awards in 2018. With more than 87 million copies sold, Red Dead 2 is one of the top five best-selling games of all time . Rockstar's next big release is GTA 6 , which launches in November for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Given the immense critical and commercial success of the Red Dead series, a third game from Rockstar (or actually fourth, counting Red Dead Revolver) is expected sometime down the road, but definitely not soon.

title: Lies Of P’s Wizard Of Oz Tease May Have Just Gotten A Lot More Interesting
text: Lies of P was a big hit when it was first released, and several years after it was confirmed that a sequel was in development , a new trademark by developer Neowiz has popped up online. As spotted on the European Union Intellectual Property Office website (via ThePhraseMaker ), the studio has registered a trademark for " Wonders of O ," suggesting that the game will put own macabre spin on L. Frank Baum's The Wonderful Wizard of Oz books. The listing is for "interactive multimedia software for playing games," but beyond that, no other details on the game can be gleaned from the registration. Lies of P had previously hinted at a trip to the Emerald City; in the mid-credits sequence, a familiar pair of ruby-red shoes could be seen. Neowiz will have free rein to put a souls-like twist on the book--which entered the public domain in 1956--since the original story includes all manner of fantastical creatures. From flying monkeys to the Tin Man, the Wicked Witch of the East and the manipulative Wizard of Oz himself, there's plenty to work with here--and we've got a few ideas of our own for where Agent P can travel to next. Following the launch of the game in 2023, Neowiz continued its twisted rendition of Pinocchio with the Overture expansion in 2025. A prequel, the expansion shed light on the events that led to the Puppet Frenzy massacre and subsequent collapse of the city of Krat. The game also came to Switch 2 earlier this year. Neowiz has periodically spoken about its approach to crafting a Lies of P sequel, and in January, the developer said it was exploring how technology-based solutions , like AI, could be used to "automate routine operational tasks" during game development. While the use of generative AI in games is a controversial topic in the West, in countries like South Korea it's actively used and considered an essential set of tools. "By processing data faster, our teams will arrive at better, more informed strategic decisions on how best to support our developers and engage with our community," Neowiz co-CEO Sean Kim said.

title: Diablo 5 Will Have The Most Classes Of Any Game In The Series
text: Diablo 5 will launch with more classes than any other game in the franchise, according to game director Joe Shely. Shely revealed more details about what to expect from Diablo 5's launch roster during a BlizzCon 2026 panel, following the game's surprise reveal (and Spring 2029 release window) as part of BlizzCon's opening ceremony . During the panel, Blizzard revealed three of Diablo 5's classes : Monk, Demon Hunter, and the new Plague Knight. "Diablo 5 is going to launch with more classes than ever before," Shely said. "And I don't just mean more classes than another Diablo game at ship. I mean more classes total." That means Blizzard is aiming for nine or 10 classes in Diablo 5 at launch, depending on whether or not they are counting Diablo 4's newly revealed Amazon class . https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y8HaSFXR7tU Shely elaborated on how the team was viewing classes, and the number of them coming right out the gate, in a group interview attended by GameSpot at BlizzCon. "What that does...it allows us to, if you started playing Diablo in Diablo 3, you probably know the Demon Hunter, and you can jump into Diablo 5 and have an experience that's familiar and new at the same time," Shely said. "It's a new representation of the class. It's going to be different, but you're still going to have twin crossbows. We're going to pay off that nostalgia you have and that feeling of what that experience was like. Having a lot of classes lets us do that in a way we haven't been able to do before. It also affords us the opportunity to explore new classes like the Plague Knight." With work on Diablo 5 in full swing, Blizzard confirmed Diablo 4 won't receive new expansions going forward. It will, however, continue to receive new seasonal content. Season of Hell's Legacy goes live September 15 and sees the return of Deckard Cain. The iconic Horadrim from previous Diablo games will task players with taking on echoes of the Prime Evils, including Diablo himself. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-FfJppNJsNY&t=7s
